full_judgment:
6. After issuance of the Rule, Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, learned Advocate, appearing for the respondent No. 1, Anti-Corruption Commission by fling an Affidavit-in-Compliance stated that they have conducted the investigation of this case and during investigation found that the petitioner is liable for abetting an office under sections 420/467/ 468/471/109 of Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 while he was discharging his duties as Appeal Officer under Rule 33 of the Tenancy Rule, 1995. It is further stated that One Gul Bahar Begum, wife of Saidur Rahman as complainant filed a petition of complaint on 23-10-2013 before the Judicial Magistrate, 5th Court, Sylhet being Complaint Case No. 33 of 2013 under sections 419/420/406/467/468/471/109 of the Penal Code against 5 persons. The learned Senior Judicial Magistrate, 2nd Court, Sylhet forwarded the said complaint petition to the Companiganj Police Station, Sylhet to take necessary steps after treating the complaint as First Information Report (FIR). Accordingly, Companiganj Police Station Case No. 23 dated 24-11-2013 under sections 419/420/406/467/ 468/471/109 of the Penal Code was started. (Annexure-I and II affidavit-in-compliance on behalf of the ACC). As the sections as mentioned above are the schedule offence of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 (shortly the ACC Act, 2004), the Officer-in-Charge of Companiganj Police Station vide letter dated 7-5-2014 requested Police Super, Sylhet to take necessary steps for forwarding the case to the Anti-Corruption Commission (in brief the ACC) for investigation. (Annexure- III affidavit in compliance on behalf of the ACC). 

 12. Mr Kollol next submits that in view of the provision of section 77 of the State Acquisition Tenancy Act and Rule 39 of Tenancy Act, and State Acquisition Tenancy Rules, 1955 respondent No. 2, Ranojit Kumar Kormoker, had no authority to arrest and prosecute the petitioner because the petitioner being Assistant Settlement Officer, Ajmirigonj, Sylhet acted as a status of judge. 

 28. It further appears that the investigation officer after completing all legal formalities and having approval from the ACC during investigation arrested the accused-writ petitioner on 19-10-2016 but the petitioner in the writ petition has not disclosed any of the facts as stated above rather it appears that the petitioner willfully suppressed the facts and misleading the court obtained the instant Rule. It further appears that the petitioner filed the instant writ petition challenging the inaction of the respondent No. 1 to take appropriate action against respondent No. 2 but it is surprising that the petitioner never served any notice/ letter seeking justice upon respondent No.1. It also appears that the sections mentioned in the FIR fall within the purview of the ACC Act, 2004 and accordingly the officer-in-charge sent the said case to the higher authority for investigation of the case by the ACC but it is utter surprising that the Companiganj Police station without having any authority investigated case and submitted charge-sheet without forwarding the name of the petitioner.
